articles.title: Conduce borracho, drogado y sin carné, quiere atropellar a dos guardias civiles y provoca un accidente frontal
articles.standfirst: Los hechos han sucedido en Torvizcón (Granada), y el conductor ha quedado en libertad con cargos a la espera de que avancen las investigaciones judiciales
articles.summary: Los hechos han sucedido en Torvizcón (Granada), y el conductor ha quedado en libertad con cargos a la espera de que avancen las investigaciones judiciales
articles.body: La Guardia Civil ha detenido a un joven de 20 años al que ya se está investigando por presuntos delitos de atentado contra agentes de la autoridad y conducción temeraria, además de bajo la influencia de alcohol y drogas. Los hechos sucedieron el pasado 4 de septiembre, cuando una patrulla de la Guardia Civil de Torvizcón (Granada) observó cómo el conductor de un Seat Ibiza blanco circulaba por la A-358 haciendo maniobras imprudentes e invadiendo el carril contrario. Cuando los agentes le dieron el alto, el conductor no hizo caso del aviso y emprendió la huida a toda velocidad. Cuando una segunda patrulla trató de interceptarlo en el cruce de las carreteras A-348 y A-346, el conductor investigado trató presuntamente de atropellar a los dos agentes que se encontraban al pie de la carretera. uno de ellos consiguió evitar el atropello refugiándose tras un muro, mientras que el otro retrocedió y sacó su arma para disuadir al conductor, que sin embargo siguió en su huida. Pero la aventura del conductor ahora investigado no llegó mucho más allá, porque 500 metros después, cuando marchaba en dirección a Vélez de Benaudalla, invadió el carril contrario y chocó frontalmente contra otro coche, cuyos ocupantes por suerte salieron ilesos. Fue ya al ser trasladado a dependencias de la Guardia Civil de Órgiva cuando se comprobó que el conductor daba positivo en alcohol y drogas, además de que carecía del carné de conducir. El detenido ha pasado a disposición del Juzgado de Guardia de Órgiva este 7 de septiembre, tras lo cual ha quedado en libertad con cargos a la espera de que continúen las investigaciones judiciales.

articles.title: Way-Too-Early Way-Too-Early 2026 Norris Trophy Rankings for NHL Best Defenseman
articles.summary: When it comes to the NHL's individual awards, there might not be a more polarizing award than the Norris Trophy, which is handed out every year to the league's best all-around defenseman.
articles.body:
When it comes to the NHL's individual awards, there might not be a more polarizing award than the Norris Trophy, which is handed out every year to the league's best all-around defenseman.

The controversy tends to center on how the position should be evaluated, how much offense and point production should factor into the voting, and whether it is even possible to assign an accurate, tangible value to defensive contributions.

Sometimes the best defense is a good offense.

Sometimes dominant defensive play comes from keeping the puck away from the other team.

Good defense is not necessarily about blocking shots or delivering crushing hits, because you can't do either of those things when you have the puck. And having the puck is the more desirable outcome and strategy in hockey.

This is a great time for elite defensemen in the NHL, and the past few years have seen the same names at the top of the Norris voting results. That will likely be the case again this season.

This is not a ranking of who we think are the best defensemen in the NHL right now, but rather a look at how we think the voting will play out at the end of the 2026-27 season (there can be, and probably is, a difference between those two distinctions).

So let's take a way-too-early look at the players who should figure to be near the top this season.

Moritz Seider, Detroit Red Wings. Seider should have received more Norris Trophy attention in 2025-26, and had the Red Wings made the playoffs, there would have been an argument that he deserved more MVP consideration. Heck, he probably should have, even without the playoffs. He is as solid a two-way defenseman as there is in the NHL right now.

Lane Hutson, Montreal Canadiens . He is going to score enough to be a factor in this, and he is going to do it while playing for a Stanley Cup contender in the Eastern Conference. But will the voters like his defensive game enough to put him in the top five?

Evan Bouchard, Edmonton Oilers . The same thing said about Hutson also applies to Bouchard. And in Bouchard's case, it's the same argument, if it were on steroids. Bouchard is as dynamic as any defenseman in the NHL when he has the puck on his stick, and few players can move the puck like him. Despite that, and despite the numbers (both in terms of point production and how much better the Oilers are with him on the ice versus without him), he remains a highly polarizing player who faces some intense, and at times baffling, criticism.

Matthew Schaefer, New York Islanders . His rookie season is one of the best ever for an 18-year-old defenseman, and there is good reason to believe he can (and ultimately will) build on that in year two. But will it be enough to get him into the top-five? He might need to wait a few years, but he will get there.

Adam Fox, New York Rangers . Another objectively great player who gets weirdly criticized, but there is a good chance the Rangers bounce back this season after a strong summer. After the additions of Sean Durzi and Marcus Pettersson, the Rangers now have a very strong top-four with Fox leading the way. He has a Norris Trophy on his resume and is still that level of player.

Sometimes the word "underrated" gets thrown around way too liberally in hockey, but Sanderson might still be firmly in that underrated category. Legitimately so. He's become one of the best all-around defensemen in the NHL and is set to be a cornerstone piece for the Senators for the foreseeable future.

Offensively, he has established himself as a 50-point player.

Defensively, his underlying metrics are superb, especially given the role he is generally asked to play.

Over the past two seasons, he has been on the ice for just 2.25 expected goals against per 60 minutes. That places him 10th out of 217 defenders who have logged at least 1,000 minutes of 5-on-5 ice time. It also comes with a 54 percent expected goals share, and he sees the majority of his shifts start with a defensive zone assignment.

He drives possession, he helps shut teams down, and he is an outstanding contributor on the offensive end of the ice.

He has already started to get some Norris Trophy love, coming off back-to-back top-10 finishes in the voting, and now that he is starting to enter his prime years, his best hockey should still be in front of him. That might also mean a big jump in the voting and perhaps a climb into the top-five. Especially if he can help get Ottawa back into the playoffs in the post-Brady Tkachuk era.

Hughes already has one Norris Trophy on his resume, and he is going to compete for more throughout his career. The only question is what team he will be a member of if (or when) he wins another. As of now, he is a member of the Wild and should be a key piece as they make a run at contending for the Stanley Cup. And as long as he is playing there, he is going to make them an outstanding team and a wildly exciting team with forward Kirill Kaprizov.

He's an elite skater, playmaker, and point-producer at the position, and a lot of that has, in some ways, underrated his defensive game. It's a lot better than it often gets credit for being.

He is in a contract year, and there are some big questions as to what comes next for him and the Wild.

Will they go all-in on an all-or-nothing season at the Stanley Cup with him and risk losing him for nothing but salary cap space after the season? Would they trade him in the middle of a Stanley Cup-contending season, much the same way the Colorado Avalanche traded Mikko Rantanen a season ago? Is it just a matter of time before he ends up with the New Jersey Devils and joins his brothers, Jack Hughes and Luke Hughes? Those are all big questions that are going to be lurking under the surface all season.

On the surface, he's going to keep playing at a Norris Trophy-level season.

Trades That Could Happen Before Training Camp

Dahlin has consistently worked his way up the Norris voting leaderboards over the past few years, going from 15th to sixth to third this past season. After some early-career inconsistencies, a seemingly endless run of new coaches and systems, and a lot of losing, he has really taken a starring role in recent years and has been one of the driving forces behind Buffalo's escape from the NHL's basement.

In that sense, he checks a lot of boxes for what will get the attention of Norris voters.

He will have enough offense to make headlines. If Buffalo makes the playoffs again, he is going to get a lot of credit for helping to continue to turn the franchise around. He is also playing in a popular hockey market that will attract a lot of attention.

After finishing as a runner-up in 2024-25, Werenski came back in 2025-26 and won it for the first time in his career with an 81-point season. He's topped the 20-goal, 80-point mark in back-to-back seasons, which is the type of production that puts him among the elite of the elite when it comes to defenseman production.

Not only for the modern NHL era, but for any era.

He is one of only 12 defensemen in NHL history to reach those milestones in a season at least two different times.

As long as he keeps producing offense at that level, he is going to be a factor in the voting for this award no matter what else he is doing with his game, and there is little indication that is going to stop anytime soon. He is a bright spot for the Blue Jackets and is going to have to be one of the main focal points of their offense again.

When he is healthy he is one of the best players in the league. He finally had a chance to show that the past two seasons.

Yes, this is the safe pick. It is the easy pick. But sometimes safe and easy picks are that way for a reason — and the reason is that they are also accurate.

Makar has finished in the top-10 of the Norris voting in all seven of his NHL seasons.

He has been a finalist in each of the past six seasons.

He has won it twice and been a runner-up once.

As long as he plays a full season, or anything even remotely close to that, he is going to score like a top-line forward, defend like a top-pairing defenseman, and help dictate the pace of play for one of the best teams in the league. He has the numbers, he has the name, he has the reputation, and he is going to play in every situation, in every big minute for a Stanley Cup contender.

At the very least, you can count on him being a finalist.

There is a good chance he will become the 10th defenseman in NHL history to win the Norris for a third time.

articles.title: Thoughts on a 10-5 Rangers win
articles.summary: Rangers 10, Mariners 5
articles.body:
Going on the road, entering the Mariners' house, and putting up a 10 spot? That is baseball pleasure.

Cal Quantrill gets credit for a Quality Start, giving him five such QSs in a row. I don't get it , either.

All three runs he allowed came on a two out, three run fourth inning home run by Lazaro Montes, a very large DH who the Mariners added to their active roster when rosters expanded. Quantrill served up a 2-1 Paul Lynde fastball that Montes…

I am searching my vocabulary to find a word that adequately describes what Montes did to that baseball.

It had a 116.1 mph exit velocity, and went, per Statcast, 474 feet. It was one of the farthest balls hit in the majors this year.

Montes, in his minor league career, has been a Three True Outcomes guy, someone who walks a lot, hits a lot of homers, and strikes out a ton. He struck out his first time up against Quantrill, and struck out again in the ninth inning against Adam Macko .

That homer by Montes cut the Rangers' lead to 4-3, and made for some nervousness, briefly, in Rangers fans households.

The Mariners executed an anti-shutdown inning in the top of the fifth, however, allowing five runs, two of them coming on a Wyatt Langford homer and three on a two out, three run Danny Jansen homer that swung any momentum the M's thought they were getting from the Montes homer back the other way.

That seemed to take the wind out of the Mariners' sails, as they went meekly the next three innings, only challenging again when Adam Macko entered the game in the eighth.

Macko allowed a run in the eighth and another in the ninth, with things getting a bit worrisome when the M's loaded the bases with one out (that out coming on the Montes strikeout by Macko, supra ) courtesy of a pair of singles and a Cody Freeman error. Fortunately for everyone's peace of mind, Macko got Randy Arozarena on a sacrifice fly for the second out before striking out Dominic Canzone to end the game, making all the Rangers and Rangers fans happy.

In between Quantrill and Macko, Robert Garcia made his triumphant return, needing just eight pitches to retire the side in the seventh, striking out pinch hitter Michael Arroyo on three pitches for the third out, a little exclamation point, of sorts, on Garcia's outing.

The Rangers got on M's starter Bryce Miller early, with Corey Seager homering to start the scoring off in the first, and Nicky Lopez blooping an opposite field single to bring home Wyatt Langford in the second.

Lopez was making his first start since August 19, something Dave Raymond and Mike Bascik were very excited about. He rewarded their enthusiasm by reaching base all four times he batted, going 3 for 3 with a hit by pitch, before being lifted for Freeman.

Miller was lifted in the top of the fourth, with the Rangers up 2-0, the bases loaded, two outs, and Joc Pederson due up. Lefthander Jose Ferrer was summoned from the pen to face Pederson.

Skip Schumaker, who has not been shy about pinch hitting early in games, sent Justin Foscue up to hit for Pederson.

Pinch hitting for your lefty-swinging DH in the fourth inning of a game opens you up for criticism if it doesn't work.

On the other hand, in a bases loaded, two out situation and with the opportunity to break the game open, you can see why Schumaker would be willing to pull the trigger and send up Foscue, rather than having Pederson deal with a lefty.

Foscue came through with a two run single, and thus the Rangers had a 4-0 lead rather than a 2-0 lead when Montes hit his homer in the bottom of the inning, and probably it didn't matter in the long run, what with the Rangers scoring a bunch of runs in the top of the fifth, but it certainly didn't hurt that the Montes bomb didn't give the Mariners the lead. Vibes, momentum, whathaveyou.

Sadly, the Guardians and Astros also both won on the road, so the Rangers are still a game and a half back of Cleveland in the Wild Card race and two games back of Houston .

Still, better to tread water than lose ground.

Cal Quantrill hit 95.3 mph with his fastball, averaging 94.1 mph, and 96.2 with his sinker, averaging 94.3 mph. Robert Garcia touched 94.6 mph with his fastball. Adam Macko's fastball reached 95.7 mph.

Wyatt Langford had a 107.3 mph home run. Corey Seager had a 106.9 mph home run. Evan Carter had a 104.2 mph single and a 100.9 mph groundout.

The Rangers need to keep this going to stay in the race. Let's do that.

articles.title: Luke Shaw training no-show mystery solved as injury fears put to bed
articles.summary: 1 Ahead of Manchester United’s clash with Everton, whispers suggested Luke Shaw might not be fit enough to feature.Yet he made himself available and played a...
articles.body:
Ahead of Manchester United 's clash with Everton , whispers suggested Luke Shaw might not be fit enough to feature.

Yet he made himself available and played a full 76 minutes.

Shaw delivered a much sharper performance, linking up with Marcus Rashford to make United's left flank a constant threat and silencing his doubters with a reassuring display.

Indeed, if he can produce that showing week after week, he will continue to quieten the critics.

Interestingly, as fans await another strong performance from Shaw in United's Champions League matchday one fixture against Sabah Baku, a worrying update has emerged from Carrington.

Daily Mail reporter Chris Wheeler, who attended the Red Devils' open training session, reported :

"Luke Shaw isn't training with the group at Carrington."

This was precisely the kind of news United supporters had dreaded this season. Shaw proved Mr Available last term, starting every single Premier League game.

Few expected him to repeat that feat this campaign, which is why INEOS rightly pursued left-back signings to share the workload on the left flank.

Those efforts ultimately failed, however, leaving Shaw as the club's only preferred option at left-back.

Now, just three games into the season, the 20-time English champions face the real threat of heading into a matchday squad without their first-choice left-back.

An injury at this stage would prove hugely frustrating.

Fortunately, while Wheeler raised that concerning Carrington update, Samuel Luckhurst has quickly calmed the worries surrounding Shaw's absence.

articles.title: Arsenal to wear uncommon kit combination in Napoli clash
articles.summary: Arsenal are set to wear an all-red kit on Wednesday night against Napoli, ditching the usual white shorts with the red shirt for the first time since 2022.Ph...
articles.body:
Arsenal are set to wear an all-red kit on Wednesday night against Napoli , ditching the usual white shorts with the red shirt for the first time since 2022.

Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

Arsenal's home kit typically includes a red-and-white shirt, white shorts, and red or white socks, and the 2026/27 campaign is no exception to that.

But whilst Arsenal will wear their home shirt in Wednesday night's Champions League opener against Napoli , they won't wear their usual home shorts.

That's according to Arsenal Shirt Collection , who report that for the first time since 2022, Arsenal will be wearing all red.

UEFA are stricter about kit clashes than other competition organisers, and Napoli's home kit uses white shorts as well. As a result, Arsenal have had to swap to red for the away game.

As mentioned, this isn't the first time this has happened, with Arsenal wearing all red for a match against Watford in 2022.

In fact, Arsenal also wore all red in a previous match against Napoli in 2019, when Alexandre Lacazette scored to send the Gunners to the Europa League semi-finals.

Prior to those two fixtures, Arsenal had also worn all red in a match against West Bromwich Albion in 2017. Across those three games, Arsenal won two and drew one, so they'll want to keep that positive record going in Wednesday's fixture.

articles.title: Daily Bean: Minten Extension; Crosby Negotiating; Red Wings Contract Problem
articles.summary: The Boston Bruins locked in a 22-year-old center, hit the ice yesterday, and are hitting the links today. Hockey season […]
articles.body:
The Boston Bruins locked in a 22-year-old center, hit the ice yesterday, and are hitting the links today.

Hockey season is right around the corner.

The Bruins made a long-term commitment and signed Fraser Minten to a seven-year deal. The Seventh Player Award winner had 35 points during his rookie season, and the two sides got the deal done before Minten's second training camp with the team.

The Bruins also announced details for rookie camp and the prospects showcase taking place in Buffalo .

Elsewhere around the league, Sidney Crosby talked about his future, and an RFA in Detroit is finding himself in a tough contract situation as camp approaches. There's more on Quinn Hughes ' negotiations, and nobody is keeping a closer eye on it than the Devils. Brady Tkachuk also spoke yesterday, as did some of his old teammates in Ottawa , and they talked about Tkachuk's departure.

Aside from Minten's extension, there were two more signings and a PTO handed out.

Happy Wednesday. Go Pats. Catch up on Bruins and league news in today's Daily Bean :

MINTEN : Bang. The Bruins are back in business, and Fraser Minten is sticking around through the 2033-34 season. Yesterday morning, the Bruins announced a seven-year, $50.4 million deal ($7.2M AAV) for the 22-year-old.

The contract includes a 16-team no-trade clause for the 2032-33 season and a 10-team no-trade clause for 2033-34.

Minten is coming off a 35-point season, and he has 40 points in 100 career NHL games. With the rising cap, the Bruins are following league trends and committing long-term to a younger player.

Boston Bruins (video via YouTube) : Minten spoke after yesterday's captains' practice. He said he got the sense an offer was coming after the exit meetings, talked about committing for seven years and earning "respect through your actions, not through your contract."

PROSPECTS : That's not all. The Bruins announced the roster for rookie camp, as well as the schedule and streaming information for the pair of games in Buffalo on Sunday and Monday. There are 16 prospects within the organization and seven invites.

Friday, Sept. 11: Warrior Ice Arena – 10:15 AM

Saturday, Sept. 12: Warrior Ice Arena – 9:30 AM

Today marks the 23rd annual Boston Bruins Foundation Golf Tournament, while the Bruins return to Warrior Ice Arena for captains' practice tomorrow.

The NHL also announced an updated start time for the Bruins' home game against the Avalanche on December 1, which follows Patrice Bergeron's jersey retirement ceremony . Instead of 7:30 PM, the game will now start at 8:00 PM.

Sportsnet : Sidney Crosby is entering the final year of his deal, but he's not stopping here. His agent is currently talking to Kyle Dubas, and Crosby fully expects to be at training camp in 2027. Luke Fox has more from Crosby, who was at the NHL's Player Media Tour in Nevada.

Detroit Hockey Now : The Red Wings need to sign Simon Edvinsson . The Red Wings do not have a GM or a president. Nobody is talking to the 23-year-old; he can't negotiate a deal! He will be at training camp, even if he remains unsigned; to his knowledge, he is footing the insurance bill.

Edvinsson also told a Swedish outlet that there has been "some interest from other clubs" regarding an offer sheet, but he wants to stay in Detroit.

New Jersey Hockey Now : The Devils are keeping a close eye on the Quinn Hughes contract negotiations in Minnesota . Chris Johnston shared his understanding of the situation on TSN 1050, and it appears that Minnesota wants to get a deal done and the money is there, but Hughes has not made up his mind.

Sportsnet : Brady Tkachuk talked about leaving Ottawa, but didn't give Senators fans too many answers as to why he left. He called it a hard decision, one he kept close to the vest, and that left many of his old teammates, including Jake Sanderson , surprised.

TSN : The Carolina Hurricanes signed defenseman Pierre-Olivier Joseph to a one-year deal worth $850K. Joseph had one goal and six points in 31 games with the Vancouver Canucks last season.

TSN : The San Jose Sharks brought goaltender Ilya Samsonov back to North America on a one-year deal. Samsonov spent last season with HC Sochi (KHL) and finished with a 3-8-0 record, 3.27 GAA, and .903 SV%.

Alex Daugherty (via 𝕏) : The Nashville Predators signed Tyson Jost to a PTO. He had 16 points (8-8–16) in 69 games with Nashville last season, and he has 165 points (69-96–165) through his 564-game NHL career.

Friday, September 11: Rookie Camp opens – Warrior Ice Arena, Brighton, MA

Sun, Sept 13-Mon, Sept 14: Prospects Showcase – LECOM Harborcenter, Buffalo, NY

articles.title: Jalen Duren could force his way out of Detroit amid contract dispute
articles.summary: Is Jalen Duren his own worst enemy in contract negotiations?
articles.body:
Many NBA rosters underwent major changes this offseason. Some teams made moves that pushed them into playoff contention, while others took a step backward and shifted their focus toward the future. With most teams having finalized their rosters, the Detroit Pistons are one of the few teams still facing an important decision before the season begins.

The Pistons are coming off a spectacular season in which they finished first in the Eastern Conference. However, one of the key players behind their success has yet to sign a contract extension.

Mar 3, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren (0) dribbles beside Cleveland Cavaliers center Jarrett Allen (31) in the first quarter at Rocket Arena. Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images

Jalen Duren, the Pistons' starting center, had an impressive regular season, earning All-NBA Third Team honors. That gave Duren the opportunity to sign a max extension worth up to five years and $287 million.

But Duren's production dropped significantly once the playoffs began. He went from averaging 19 points and 10 rebounds during the regular season to 10 points and eight rebounds in the postseason. That decline has made Detroit hesitant to commit to a massive contract.

The Pistons are reportedly willing to offer Duren a five-year, $35 million deal, but Duren and his camp believe his regular-season performance earned him a max contract. Neither side appears willing to budge, creating a stalemate between the team and its starting center.

Apr 22, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren (0) reacts during the second half against the Orlando Magic during game two of the first round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images

If the two sides can't reach an agreement, Duren has two options. He could be included in a sign-and-trade or accept a $9.6 million qualifying offer that would make him a free agent in 2027.

However, the Pistons have reportedly told Duren and his camp that they will not include him in a sign-and-trade. That leaves Duren with one option if the two sides can't agree: signing the $9.6 million qualifying offer.

Duren and the Pistons have until Sept. 30 to reach an agreement. Although they have said they won't trade him, he could force their hand if he continues to play hardball.

articles.title: Byron Young shares video inside Rams' incredibly luxurious flight to Australia
articles.summary: Safe to say, the Rams will be comfortable on their flight to Australia, taking a double-decker plane from L.A. to Melbourne.
articles.body:
Flying 16 hours from Los Angeles to Australia isn't easy for anyone, but it's not as if the Rams are jamming their players into tiny coach seats. They're obviously taking their own flight to Melbourne, making everyone as comfortable as possible.

Sean McVay said every player would have a lay-flat bed , with the goal that they will sleep most of the way and be fresh after arriving in Melbourne. Needless to say, it won't be very difficult for them to get comfortable on the flight.

They took off on Tuesday night and Byron Young shared a video from inside the incredibly luxurious plane – which has two floors to spread passengers out.

The Rams will arrive in Australia on Thursday morning before kicking off against the 49ers on Friday at 10:35 a.m. local time.

articles.title: Colts depth chart: What Ravens fans need to know for Week 1
articles.summary: Indianapolis’ depth chart features an explosive offense and formidable secondary that could create significant challenges for Baltimore in Week 1
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts released their first unofficial depth chart of the 2026 regular season ahead of Sunday's opener against the Baltimore Ravens at Lucas Oil Stadium. Daniel Jones will lead an offense featuring Jonathan Taylor , Tyler Warren , Alec Pierce , Josh Downs and Keenan Allen . Indianapolis also strengthened its defense with Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward Sr., giving coordinator Lou Anarumo one of the NFL's most accomplished outside cornerback tandems.

The depth chart remains unofficial, but it provides Ravens fans with a clearer picture of the personnel Baltimore will face in Week 1.

Daniel Jones has an impressive collection of weapons

Indianapolis has surrounded Jones with enough talent to stress every level of Jesse Minter's defense.

Taylor remains the centerpiece after rushing for 1,585 yards and 18 touchdowns last season. Warren led the Colts in targets as a rookie and gives Jones a 6-foot-6 receiving option in the middle of the field. Pierce is one of the NFL's most dangerous vertical receivers, while Downs can create separation from the slot. Allen provides experience, route-running ability, and another dependable option on third down.

Baltimore cannot focus its attention entirely on Taylor without creating opportunities for Jones in the passing game.

Tyler Warren is the clear No. 1 tight end.

Warren is listed ahead of Mo Alie-Cox and Drew Ogletree after quickly establishing himself as one of Indianapolis' most important offensive players. His size, athleticism, and versatility could require Baltimore to use Kyle Hamilton in coverage. Minter can also rotate Malaki Starks , Jaylinn Hawkins and the linebackers into the matchup.

Preventing Warren from controlling the middle of the field will be one of Baltimore's most important defensive assignments.

Jalen Travis gets the first opportunity at right tackle

Indianapolis lists Travis at right tackle, with Luke Tenuta behind him.

That matchup should attract the attention of Trey Hendrickson , Mike Green and Baltimore's other pass rushers. The Ravens can move Hendrickson across the formation to identify favorable matchups and test Indianapolis' protection plan. The Colts still have proven interior blockers in Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner's namesake? No—Nelson and center Tanor Bortolini—but Baltimore should attack the less-established right side of the line.

Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward present a major test

Indianapolis' defense may be strongest at outside cornerback.

Gardner can eliminate space and challenge receivers at the line of scrimmage. Ward gives Anarumo another experienced defender who can handle difficult assignments on the perimeter. Their presence could allow Indianapolis to use additional defenders against Jackson and Henry. Zay Flowers , Rashod Bateman and Baltimore's other receivers must consistently win isolated matchups.

Justin Walley is listed as the starting nickel cornerback, creating a potential matchup for Flowers when Baltimore moves him inside.

The Colts have a disruptive defensive front.

Buckner and Stewart anchor the interior, while Latu and Key provide pressure from the edge.

That group will immediately test Baltimore's rebuilt offensive line. Jovaughn Gwyn is making his first career start at center, while rookie Vega Ioane will start at right guard. Keeping Jackson comfortable and creating running lanes for Henry will require strong communication from a line playing its first regular-season game together.

Anthony Richardson is the backup quarterback.

Jones is the unquestioned starter, while Richardson is listed second and Riley Leonard third. Indianapolis could still create a package for Richardson because of his size and rushing ability. Baltimore must be prepared for the possibility, particularly in short-yardage or red-zone situations.

The primary challenge remains Jones, but Richardson's presence gives the Colts another potential wrinkle.

articles.title: Browns star joins Cleveland Guardians ownership group
articles.summary: He joins Cleveland Heights native and Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, who was announced as a fellow Guardians' minority investor back in May.
articles.body:
CLEVELAND (WKBN) -- Cleveland Browns five-time Pro Bowl cornerback Denzel Ward has joined the ownership group of the Cleveland Guardians as a minority investor in the franchise.

He joins Cleveland Heights native and Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, who was announced as a fellow Guardians' minority investor back in May.

"Cleveland is my hometown. I'm so blessed to be able to show up for this city on the field and now as a part of the Guardians organization," Ward said. "I couldn't be more grateful to the Dolan family and David Blitzer for the opportunity to continue to pour into this community and give back to the best fans in the world."

Ward is a native of Macedonia, Ohio and a graduate of Nordonia High School. He played college football at Ohio State, before being selected in the first round, at No. 4 overall, in the 2018 NFL Draft.

He recently signed a two-year contract extension with the Browns that will keep him with the team through the 2029 season.

"Denzel Ward is a hometown hero on the field and off it," Paul Dolan, Guardians Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and David Blitzer, Guardians Vice Chairman, said. "His excellence, character and commitment to this community – including his work with the Make Them Know Your Name Foundation – make him a perfect fit for our organization. We are proud to welcome him as a partner in the Guardians future."

According to a release from the Guardians, Ward will be honored at Progressive Field on Tuesday, September 15 at a game against the Chicago White Sox.

Formula 1 is heading to the brand-new Madring in Madrid this weekend for the Spanish Grand Prix - the final European round of the 2026 season.

The sport's newest track will play host to the Spanish capital's first F1 race since Jarama around 40 years ago, and it is set to present a unique challenge for all drivers with its fast layout featuring the longest banked corner on the calendar - 547 meters long and a 24% gradient.

Mercedes' Andrea Kimi Antonelli arrives at the weekend with his sights set on another victory to inch closer to his maiden drivers' title. Just a few days ago, the Italian youngster pulled off a sensational win from 19th on the grid at his home race in Monza, further extending his championship lead over teammate and closest rival George Russell by 66 points.

Russell on the other hand will be hoping to stand at the top of the podium after watching his third win of the season slip away in Italy. The Briton was jumped by Antonelli with only four laps remaining, eventually crossing the line around four seconds behind in P2.

Lewis Hamilton , having celebrated his first grand prix win in Ferrari red a few months ago in Barcelona, is keen on adding another win on Spanish soil, while his teammate Charles Leclerc is hoping to bounce back after a tough Monza outing where he crashed heavily out of the race on lap 2.

Defending champion Lando Norris is just another driver eyeing victory at F1's newest venue - one that would cut his 96-point deficit to leader Antonelli in the standings.

On a different note, Isack Hadjar remains sidelined at Red Bull due to a wrist injury he picked up during the summer break. He has missed races in Zandvoort, Monza and now Madrid.

Liam Lawson will once again step in for him at Red Bull, while Yuki Tsunoda takes on Lawson's seat at the sister team, Racing Bulls.

articles.title: Fantasy football start or sit Week 1: Jadarian Price, George Holani, Rashid Shaheed
articles.summary: Some fantasy football start or sit advice for Seahawks running backs Jadarian Price and George Holani, and wide receiver Rashid Shaheed.
articles.body:
Running backs Jadarian Price and George Holani and wide receiver Rashid Shaheed will all be in the lineup for the Seattle Seahawks when they begin the 2026 NFL season on Wednesday night against the New England Patriots .

The Seahawks are turning the page to a new era in the backfield after allowing Super Bowl MVP and running back Kenneth Walker to leave to the Kansas City Chiefs in free agency.

One of the players returning from last season is running back Zach Charbonnet , but he is on physically unable to perform list as he continues to recover from a torn ACL and will miss at least the first four games.

That leaves the backfield work to Price and Holani, and Emmanuel Wilson could mix in, also.

So, who is the better start in fantasy football between Price and Holani? And is Shaheed worthy of a spot in your lineup in Week 1?

We answer those questions with our start or sit advice for all three players.

Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price (8) during the first training camp at Virginia Mason Athletic Center. Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Price was the Seahawks' first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft and the belief is that he will lead the backfield in Week 1, according to ESPN's Brady Henderson , who also notes that fellow back, George Holani , will be involved as well.

"The best guess is that the Seahawks are planning, for now, to roll with (Jadarian) Price as their lead back while mixing in a heavy dose of George Holani, whose receiving and pass-blocking skills seem perfectly suited for third-down work," Henderson wrote.

With the expectation that Price is likely to at least be in control of early-down work, he should garner enough volume to return solid flex value in Week 1.

Seattle Seahawks running back George Holani (36) during minicamp at Virginia Mason Athletic Center. Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Holani is listed as the No. 1 back on the depth chart , but based on Henderson's note above, it looks like he's going to mostly be on the field on third downs.

Without a ton of certainty, it's hard to trust a back like Holani who may be fully dependent on receiving production.

The veteran should be left on the bench in Week 1.

Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (22) during minicamp at Virginia Mason Athletic Center. Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Shaheed was brought over in a trade deadline deal with the New Orleans Saints last season and the Seahawks decided to bring him back this offseason.

Shaheed had a few good games with Seattle in the regular season in 2025, with four catches for 67 yards in one game and five catches for 74 yards in another.

Outside of those two contests, Shaheed didn't do much, tallying 125 yards on 18 catches over his other 10 games (including playoffs).

From Week 10 through Week 18, Shaheed ranked as WR61 overall, per Fantasy Pros .

Keep Shaheed out of starting lineups in Week 1.

articles.title: Ravens vs. Colts: Five keys to a Week 1 victory for Baltimore
articles.summary: The Ravens open a new era Sunday, but the formula for success against the Colts remains fairly straightforward.
articles.body:
Months of work and preparation have led us to another season. It's been a while since we've seen Baltimore Ravens football that counts. We've discussed Jesse Minter's new era and atmosphere until we're blue in the face. We've made predictions about Declan Doyle's work ethic and innovative offense .

Now comes another season of lofty expectations. The Indianapolis Colts enter Week 1 carrying ambitions of their own. They collapsed during the second half of last season after an 8-2 start, but Shane Steichen's team remains talented enough to challenge anyone when things are clicking.

Season openers rarely unfold exactly as expected. New coordinators unveil wrinkles that haven't appeared on film. Players settle first-game nerves. Momentum swings unexpectedly. Baltimore doesn't need a perfect performance to begin the season 1-0, but several areas could go a long way toward determining whether the Ravens leave Week 1 with a victory. Here are a few.

Establish defensive dominance in the trenches early

Few matchups will have a greater impact on Sunday's outcome than the battle along the line of scrimmage. The Colts feature one of the NFL's premier running backs in Jonathan Taylor , a player who in many ways resembles Derrick Henry because he combines power, vision, and game-breaking speed.

Limiting Taylor's effectiveness on early downs would force Indianapolis into less favorable situations and place more pressure on Daniel Jones . On the other side of the ball, Baltimore's offensive line must create room for Henry while handling a defensive front led by DeForest Buckner , Grover Stewart , and Laiatu Latu . If the Ravens consistently win at the point of attack, several other keys on this list become much easier to achieve.

The Ravens don't need Lamar Jackson to play superhero football in Week 1. They need him available for four quarters. Indianapolis added talent to every level of its defense and possesses multiple pass rushers capable of creating problems.

Latu led the Colts in sacks last season, while Buckner remains one of the league's most disruptive interior defenders. Arden Key and Adetomiwa Adebawore add even more athleticism to the front. Baltimore's offensive line enters the season opener with Jovaughn Gwyn expected to start at center, making communication and protection adjustments even more important. Keeping Jackson clean won't guarantee victory, but consistent pressure dramatically increases the difficulty.

Opening-day football often comes down to execution in critical moments. Both teams possess enough offensive firepower to move the football between the 20-yard lines. The question is which team capitalizes when scoring opportunities arrive. Baltimore would love to see Henry's physical running style and Jackson's creativity create problems near the goal line.

Defensively, the Ravens must prevent Indianapolis from turning promising drives into touchdowns. Field goals are easier to survive. Touchdowns change games. If Baltimore wins the battle inside the red zone, it may ultimately win the battle on the scoreboard.

Generate explosive plays on offense and eliminate them on defense.

This was one of Minter's most frequently discussed points throughout training camp. The Ravens have explosive-play potential all over the field. Jackson can create chunk gains with his arm or legs. Zay Flowers remains one of the league's most dangerous open-field weapons. Rashod Bateman and Ja'Kobi Lane provide downfield threats capable of changing field position in a single snap.

The challenge is preventing Indianapolis from doing the same. Taylor remains capable of turning a routine handoff into a long touchdown run, while Alec Pierce has developed a reputation as one of the NFL's better vertical threats. Explosive plays can erase otherwise solid football. Baltimore needs to create them more often than it allows them.

It isn't the flashiest key, but it may be one of the most important. Week 1 games often feel sloppier than contests played later in the season. Drives stall. Opportunities are missed. Points become precious. Baltimore enters the season with Tyler Loop expected to handle kicking duties, and every scoring opportunity could prove significant.

The Colts averaged 31 points in their eight victories last season and showed they can stress opposing defenses when their offense finds rhythm. If Sunday's opener turns into the type of one-possession game that Ravens fans know all too well, special teams could determine the outcome.

The Ravens don't need to unveil every wrinkle of Declan Doyle's offense or play a flawless football game to begin the season with a victory. They do, however, need to control the areas that most often decide close games.

If Baltimore wins the battle up front, protects Lamar Jackson, executes in the red zone, creates more explosive plays than it allows, and capitalizes on scoring opportunities, the Ravens should give themselves an excellent chance to leave Week 1 with a 1-0 record. In a conference as competitive as the AFC, every early victory matters.

articles.title: Texans sign former Iowa QB Mark Gronowski to practice squad
articles.summary: Mark Gronowski has his new home. The Houston Texans signed the former Iowa signal-caller to their practice squad.
articles.body:
After a whirlwind month of August for former Iowa football quarterback Mark Gronowski , where he was cut and re-signed multiple times by the Miami Dolphins , the 6-foot-2, 227-pounder has found a new home in the NFL.

In Houston , he figures to serve as the emergency third quarterback behind starter C.J. Stroud and backup Davis Mills . An emergency third quarterback must be on the 53-man roster or as one of two standard practice squad elevations per week. An elevated quarterback would have to be active for the game rather than in the emergency role. A player can be activated three times per season.

During his two preseason appearances with the Dolphins, Gronkowski was 6 for 13 passing for 98 yards and added 37 yards on the ground in 41 offensive snaps.

In his lone season at Iowa , Gronowski passed for 1,741 yards and 10 touchdowns and ran for an additional 545 yards and 16 scores. The Hawkeyes posted a 9-4 (6-3 Big Ten) record last season with Gronowski under center.

After second-year and former Wisconsin Badger quarterback Graham Mertz suffered a torn ACL in the preseason opener against the Los Angeles Chargers , the Texans needed to find depth options under center. Following initial roster cutdowns, Houston was the league's only team not to carry a third option on its initial practice squad.

articles.title: Official police statements released on ‘The Butcher’ Andy Williams’ death
articles.summary: AEW wrestler and band guitarist, ‘The Butcher’ Andy Williams, recently passed away at the age of 48. Williams collapsed after his match at the Enjoy Wrestli...
articles.body:
AEW wrestler and band guitarist, 'The Butcher' Andy Williams, recently passed away at the age of 48 . Williams collapsed after his match at the Enjoy Wrestling event near Pittsburgh on Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026.

Shortly after, Fightful reported that paramedics used a defibrillator and performed chest compressions before he was eventually taken away in an ambulance. Later, on Sunday, Sept. 6, 2026, TMZ reported and confirmed Williams' death.

Now, the Millvale Police Department has shared its official statement with POST Wrestling. "At approximately 8:45 p.m. on Saturday, September 5th, 2026, Millvale Borough Police officers were dispatched to Mr. Smalls Theatre for a report of a male wrestler who had struck his head on a ring post during a wrestling event.

"Upon arrival, officers located Andy Williams unresponsive and being attended to by two physicians who were at the venue with the wrestling organization. Shortly before the arrival of Ross/West View EMS, Williams stopped breathing. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) was initiated, and an automated external defibrillator (AED) was applied.

"Upon the arrival of Ross/West View EMS, life-saving measures were continued. Williams was transported by EMS to Allegheny General Hospital, where he was pronounced deceased at approximately 9:43 p.m.," the statement read.

It further claimed that there were no visible signs of trauma or any indications of foul play. As of now, the official cause and manner of Williams' death remain pending. An autopsy has been performed by the Allegheny County Medical Examiner's Office. The final determination of the cause of Williams' death will be made after the results of the examination are out.

Williams was a professional wrestler and the guitarist for Atomic Rule. While actively wrestling on the independent circuit, "The Butcher" was popularly known for his run with AEW, as well as his tag team with Blade. The duo was part of the AEW roster from 2019 to 2026. Williams also enjoyed a celebrated musical career, where he was part of the band Every Time I Die.

articles.title: Jets at Titans: 5 things to watch for during Week 1 game
articles.summary: The Jets open the 2026 regular season against the Titans on Sunday, and here are five things to watch for Week 1.
articles.body:
The wait is finally over, but the most interesting thing about the New York Jets entering Week 1 has very little to do with their record.

Everybody knows they're opening the season Sunday against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium. Everybody knows Geno Smith is back. Everybody knows Robert Saleh is standing on the opposite sideline.

What's still unknown is whether the vision head coach Aaron Glenn sold throughout the offseason will actually show up when the games start to count.

After a 3-14 season, the Jets spent months reshaping their roster, adding veterans, developing young talent, and placing significant trust in a new coaching structure. Sunday's opener will provide the first real glimpse of whether that foundation is strong enough to accelerate the franchise's timeline.

With that, here are Jets Wire's five things to watch for during the Jets' Week 1 game against the Titans :

No matter how much either side downplays it, this matchup comes with an unavoidable subplot . Saleh spent four seasons as the Jets' head coach before being dismissed during the 2024 season. After another stint as the San Francisco 49ers' defensive coordinator last season, he landed another head coaching opportunity in Tennessee.

As fate would have it, his first regular-season game with the Titans comes against the organization that gave him his first chance to lead a team.

For Saleh, this game won't define his tenure in Tennessee.

For the Jets, it won't define Glenn's future. But both sides understand the optics.

Considering how familiar the Jets would be with Saleh, does that give Gang Green any sort of advantage when facing his defense?

Perhaps the most important development Sunday won't be who is playing but who is calling the plays. Glenn has taken on a larger role with the defense, trusting what he has described as one of his strengths as a coach .

On the other side of the ball, veteran offensive coordinator Frank Reich will unveil a regular-season game plan after a preseason that revealed very little about what the Jets truly want to be offensively. The Jets have invested heavily in young talent and veteran leadership on both sides of the ball.

Now the spotlight shifts to the coaches. Scheme, adjustments, and situational decision-making often determine close games in September, and Sunday's opener should provide the first clues about how this coaching staff plans to maximize the roster it has assembled.

Can the new additions make an immediate impact?

The Jets didn't spend the offseason standing still. Veterans were added to address weaknesses, rookies were drafted with the expectation of contributing quickly and several new starters are expected to play significant roles from Day 1.

Sunday's game will be the first meaningful test of whether those moves actually improved the roster.

That includes first-round rookies Kenyon Sadiq, Omar Cooper Jr. and David Bailey, along with veteran additions expected to help stabilize areas that struggled a season ago.

Week 1 rarely tells the whole story, but it often reveals which newcomers are ready to contribute immediately and which ones still need time to develop.

What should we realistically expect from Geno Smith's return?

No one will ever forget seeing Geno Smith proclaim, "he was written off, but refused to write back." Well, following a rough one-and-done campaign with the Las Vegas Raiders , he's been written off again.

Let's hope he doesn't write back this time either. The feel-good storyline writes itself. More than a decade after the Jets drafted him in the second round, Smith is back in green and white with another opportunity to lead the franchise.

The Jets don't need Smith to carry the offense by himself. They need him to be efficient, protect the football and consistently get the ball to Garrett Wilson , Breece Hall and the rest of the team's playmakers. If he can do that, the offense has a chance to be significantly more functional than it was a year ago.

More than any statistical benchmark, Week 1 will be about command. Does Smith look comfortable? Does he look decisive? Does he look like a quarterback capable of helping the Jets win games rather than simply avoiding mistakes?

Can the Jets begin the season with a road win and a 1-0 start?

Every season opener carries added significance because nobody truly knows what a team is until the games begin. The Titans are rebuilding under Saleh, while the Jets are attempting to prove that last season's record is not an accurate reflection of their long-term trajectory. Both franchises enter the afternoon desperate to establish momentum.

For New York specifically, this feels like the kind of game a team with legitimate aspirations should win. Road games are never easy in the NFL, but the Jets have spent the offseason talking about growth, accountability, and progress. Sunday offers the first opportunity to show that those changes are more than offseason talking points.

By the time the Jets leave Nashville, the biggest takeaway may have nothing to do with Saleh's return or Smith's homecoming. The real story could be whether New York looks like a team beginning to turn the corner — or one that still has a longer climb ahead than anyone hoped.

articles.title: 5 bold predictions for the Bills offense in 2026
articles.summary: Making 5 bold predictions for the Bills offense during the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
The Bills are following up an eventful offseason and gaining steam and momentum as the start to their regular season campaign is now right around the corner.

With a new head coach who will have more freedom to call his offense in Joe Brady, the team's 2026 campaign is one of great interest to see how it will unfold.

The new role might see the offense open up more, especially with some new additions on the field. The team traded for veteran WR1 DJ Moore , and drafted several players who might make some impact in the receiver rotation like offensive lineman Jude Bowry and Zane Durant , and receiver Skyler Bell.

With Moore opening up the offense as the long missing boundary and deep threat target that can create more opportunities for the rest of the passing game and offense in the coverage he commands, and his past success in Joe Brady's offense in Carolina, big things may be in store. Maybe even a Super Bowl appearance.

With that, here are five bold predictions for the Bills offense in 2026:

Is a second MVP campaign for QB Josh Allen loading?

Allen was able to secure the award last season without some of the weapons that have been added, as well as with injuries to key pass-catchers

Moore adds an important coverage spreading element to the field that was missing last season following the departures of then WR1 Stefon Diggs and WR2 Gabe Davis . Offensive coordinator Joe Brady has a preference for outside vertical routes that create space for crossing routes, which can both increase big plays downfield while opening up more opportunities for tight end Dalton Kincaid and receivers Khalil Shakir , Keon Coleman , and Curtis Samuel , not to mention the team's trio of receiving running backs.

If he can continue to protect the ball successfully and work out whatever the late-game play calling snafus were with Brady that cost a couple of potential wins in 2024, he could find himself in line for a second consecutive most valuable player caliber season.

Moore has gone for over 1,000 yards four times in his career, most recently for Chicago in 2023 and several times in Carolina from 2019 through 2021, including twice in Brady's offense.

He and Allen have found their rhythm during the offseason program and preseason action, and it's a good sign for Allen and the rest of the targets in the passing game that Moore will open up opportunities for.

If everyone eats in Joe Brady's offense, Allen and Moore are poised to help feed them, and the Bills new WR1 could yield yet another 1,000+ yard season along the way.

Cook has only gotten better each year since Buffalo drafted him out of Georgia, and is, according to him , a "little faster on grass" referring to the new Highmark Stadium field.

The RB1 has been on a steady rise the past couple seasons, with some ground to gain under his feet as he carries the ball during Buffalo's home games and a potentially increased role in the passing game this year, he could take it to the next level.

The Bills also play four of their nine 2026 away games on natural grass fields. Week 6 at Allegiant Stadium against the Las Vegas Raiders , Week 14 at Lambeau Field against the Green Bay Packers , Week 16 at Empower Field at Mile High in a Division Round playoff rematch against the Denver Broncos , and a Week 17 Hard Rock Stadium matchup against their AFC East rival Miami Dolphins .

Coleman has produced in his limited usage over the past two seasons, although he's also missed time or been limited due to off the field tardiness and maturity growing pains have, in turn, limited his overall numbers.

That he's played in a Joe Brady "everyone eats" offense that relies on efficiency and distributes that ball around the passing game has limited the live game reps that he might normally see in another offense.

That being said, Coleman has shown playmaking abilities and potential, as well as a big game in last season's opener against the Ravens in which he was lit up on targets and catches.

He spent the offseason working out and learning from past star receivers like Stevie Johnson and Chad Ochocinco, and current Dallas Cowboys WR1 and his own relative , Ceedee Lamb .

Brady wants to elevate Coleman's role in the offense, and the young receiver knows this is a critical season for him to perform at the pro level. It would stand to reason he will be provided with and seize the opportunities to do just that, even to the extent that he comes in second in the passing game by season's end.

articles.title: Heat reportedly interested in signing $38M energetic 11-year journeyman to backup Davion Mitchell
articles.summary: The Miami Heat have one last roster spot left. It seems like they have experienced interest in a well known veteran to serve as a backup for Davion Mitchell.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat still have a big roster decision to make with their final spot. There had been some discussion about Ben Simmons potentially joining the team, but he ultimately signed with the Sacramento Kings .

"A team in win-now mode has to draw a valuation line between players who can be developed/reclaimed and those needed to be able to contribute in the moment, without questions of whether they are healthy enough or still skilled enough. The Kings make all the sense for Ben Simmons and he makes all the sense for them. There is no pressure to produce in Sacramento," Sun Sentinel's Ira Winderman wrote.

There was also some buzz surrounding Gabe Vincent , but that does not appear likely to come to fruition either.

"I do think the former Heat guard Gabe Vincent has some fans in this building and some fans on that roster who would love for him to be back into the fold, right now it's looking like Miami is not a outcome for Gabe Vincent. But I do think Miami's roster isn't exactly done and the guard position will be something they look at moving forward," Bleacher Report's Jake Fischer said.

There have been several reports about other options being on the table. According to Heavy.com's Sean Deveney, Miami has some interest in veteran point guard Cam Payne.

"The Heat have weighed the likes of veteran backups Gabe Vincent and Cam Payne, but would prefer to find someone with a better upside. They do need a placeholder for that spot, though," Deveney wrote.

Payne has been a journeyman throughout his career, playing for seven teams during his time in the NBA. The veteran guard could be a great mentor for Davion Mitchell , who has taken a big step forward this offseason.

Payne has made $38 million throughout his career. He plays with a motor that simply never seems to turn off, which could make him an intriguing option for the Heat off the bench. Adding Payne would give Miami another experienced guard while also providing some energy and leadership to the second unit.

articles.title: 49ers' Alfred Collins tears patellar tendon in Australia, out for 2026
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers defender Alfred Collins sustained a season-ending torn patellar tendon in Australia, coach Kyle Shanahan announced Wednesday.
articles.body:
Sept. 9 (UPI) -- San Francisco 49ers defensive tackle Alfred Collins sustained a torn patellar tendon at practice in Melbourne, Australia and will miss the 2026 season, coach Kyle Shanahan announced Wednesday.

Shanahan said the injury occurred at Tuesday's session. Collins missed off-season organized team activities and part of training camp while recovering from shoulder surgery.

"I'm hurting for Alfred," Shanahan told reporters. "It happened during a period right before we started going against each other. It was really unfortunate for him."

Collins, 24, appeared in 16 games, with one start, last season for the 49ers. The second-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft was slated to start alongside Osa Odighizuwa at defensive tackle.

C.J. West is now expected to fill in for Collins. Rookies Gracen Halton and James Thompson Jr. also could see an increase in action. Thompson didn't practice Tuesday due to a hamstring strain.

The 49ers will take on the Los Angeles Rams in the second game of the 2026 NFL season at 8:35 p.m. EDT Wednesday in Melbourne.

articles.body:
Alexis Mac Allister Contract Situation Raises January Questions for Liverpool

Liverpool might have expected the closing of the transfer window to bring a little calm. Instead, Alexis Mac Allister's contract situation has ensured that January already feels uncomfortably close.

Speaking alongside Trev Downey on an Anfield Index podcast, Dave Davis examined Mac Allister's comments about his Liverpool future and the consequences they could have when the transfer market reopens. The midfielder has two years remaining on his contract, but his public admission that he was disappointed not to receive a new deal has changed the conversation.

Davis highlighted Mac Allister's words: "It makes me sad I didn't get a new deal, but there is still time. I will give 100% until the last day I am here. We will see what happens."

For Liverpool, those comments have created questions that could persist all the way to January.

Mac Allister Comments Put Liverpool Under Scrutiny

Davis was particularly struck by Mac Allister's repeated expressions of disappointment and the midfielder's explanation that discussions had taken place through his representative rather than directly with him.

Mac Allister said: "There wasn't any direct conversation with me. It was with my agent. I don't want to say things that were never said, but what I got from my agent is they weren't in a position to renew me."

Davis picked out that particular wording, describing "weren't in a position to renew me" as an "interesting choice of phrase".

Mac Allister also referenced teammates who had received new contracts, saying: "I see Dominic and Ryan renewing their contracts and that makes me happy as they deserve it. But at the same time, it makes me sad as I do get mine. But there is still time."

For Davis, the timing created another issue, coming immediately before Andoni Iraola's first Champions League match as Liverpool head coach.

January Could Become Crucial for Liverpool

The most significant part of the discussion concerned what happens next.

Davis believes Mac Allister's contractual position could affect Liverpool's negotiating strength if another club makes an approach in January.

"I don't see how this helps at all cuz you're going to have a player who's going to have 18 months left on his deal in January," Davis said.

He then outlined the negotiating problem Liverpool could encounter, suggesting interested clubs could use Mac Allister's public comments and remaining contract length to reduce their offers.

Davis illustrated the point with a hypothetical example, explicitly stressing that he was inventing the figures: "We might have bid 65 million in the summer. Let's call it 45 now because that's what they can do."

His conclusion was clear: "I don't see how this Liverpool help helps us in any way in that sense."

Camara Conversation Returns to Foreground

Another name inevitably entered the discussion, Lamine Camara.

Davis referred to continuing reports surrounding Liverpool's interest in Camara and connected that discussion with the uncertainty around Mac Allister.

"Mac Allister out, Camara in. It almost feels like that's been thrown right to the forefront again, doesn't it?" he said. "And we'll be talking about this all the way to January."

Downey agreed that the situation had become complicated, while identifying the most positive possible outcome as Mac Allister rediscovering his best form and eventually earning another Liverpool contract.

Downey said: "The best case scenario here is that we get a rejuvenated Mac Allister who is actually being spoken about as a candidate for a new contract."

Davis also questioned whether a lucrative new contract would ultimately fit Liverpool's plans, particularly given Mac Allister's age relative to the club's other midfielders and the wider wage structure.

Whatever Liverpool decide, Davis believes the events surrounding Mac Allister have created an awkward business situation.

"Either way, whichever way we dress up or play this scenario, I'm not sure today was a good day for Liverpool in a business sense."

That is where Liverpool now find themselves. Mac Allister has publicly emphasised his love for the club and promised to give "100% until the last day" he remains there. His contract situation, however, is now firmly part of the discussion.

The summer window has barely disappeared from view, yet Liverpool already have another significant question waiting for them as January approaches.
